entities.title: The zazz_host import module
entities.summary: The five host functions a script's WebAssembly may import besides WASI preview 1: request_len, take, send, http and cancelled.
consumers: zazz-sdk's WebAssembly backend (macos/rust/zazz-sdk/src/wasm.rs), compiled into every Rust script
Prebuilt modules of kind "wasm" from any language, which import the functions directly
guarantees: request_len() -> i64: the length of the inbox, which holds the call message when the instance starts and the last HTTP reply after http.
take(ptr, cap) -> i64: copies up to cap bytes of the inbox into guest memory and returns how many.
send(ptr, len): a JSON message from the guest; progress goes to zazzled at once, anything else is kept, and the last result or ready message is the call's answer.

http(ptr, len) -> i64: a request in zazz-sdk's HTTP wire layout; the policy is checked first (https only, no IP literals or credentials, exact or `*.` host match), then the reply is placed in the inbox and its length returned, or minus the length of an error JSON.
cancelled() -> i32: 1 once zazzled has sent another frame (a cancel) while the call runs.
The guest must export memory and _start; any other import is refused at compile.
entities.compatibility: The import names are checked at compile time (engine.rs HOST_FUNCS), so adding a function is compatible and renaming or removing one breaks every registered script; the plan's `recv` name was not used.

entities.title: Serve mode's descriptors and control channel
entities.summary: zazz-worker serve expects its control socket on fd 3 and a module from `zazz-worker compile` on fd 4, a hello frame first, then call frames each carrying the caller's three standard streams.
consumers: zazzled's worker pool and calls (macos/rust/zazzled/src/zazz/pool.rs spawn, call.rs exchange)
guarantees: Frames are a u32 little-endian length followed by JSON (zazz-sdk proto), at most 16 MiB.
hello carries args, env, preopens [{host, guest, write}], network ("none", "all" or {hosts}), memory_mb and call_ms; it is answered by the guest's ready frame.
Every other frame is passed to a fresh instance as its message; three descriptors sent with it (SCM_RIGHTS) become the guest's stdin, stdout and stderr, otherwise the guest gets closed streams.
Each call is answered by exactly one frame: the guest's result, or an error result with code failed, timeout, out_of_memory, script_crashed or protocol, carrying the call's id.
shutdown, or the end of the stream, ends the process.
entities.compatibility: zazzled and zazz-worker ship together in every release and are found side by side, so the two sides change in the same commit; a precompiled module only loads in the zazz-worker build whose engine compiled it.
